assemble.prompt: Match each term to its definition.

items.label: Glycoprotein
items.clue: A protein with one or more carbohydrate chains covalently attached.

items.label: Cellulose
items.clue: The structural polysaccharide of plant cell walls, an unbranched polymer of beta-glucose.

items.label: Hydrophobic
items.clue: Describes a molecule or region of a molecule that does not dissolve in or associate with water.

items.label: Triglyceride
items.clue: A lipid formed when one glycerol molecule is linked by condensation reactions to three fatty acid molecules.

questions.stem: Carbon forms an enormous diversity of compounds, on which life is based. Which statement about the bonding of a single carbon atom is correct?

options.text: It forms up to four covalent bonds, single or double, with carbon or other non-metal atoms
It forms any number of covalent bonds, which is why so many carbon compounds exist
It transfers its four outer electrons to other atoms, giving charged compounds
It links to neighbouring carbon atoms by weak hydrogen bonds that are easily broken

questions.stem: Two monosaccharides are joined by a condensation reaction to form a disaccharide. What happens in this reaction?

options.text: A molecule of water is taken in and split to supply the atoms that join the monomers
A hydrogen bond forms between the two monomers, holding them together as a disaccharide
Water dissolves the two monomers so that they meet, but no water is formed or used
A covalent bond forms between the monomers and a molecule of water is released

questions.stem: A polypeptide made of 100 amino acids is completely hydrolysed into free amino acids. How many water molecules are used in the process?

options.text: 99 water molecules
100 water molecules
1 water molecule
0 water molecules

questions.explanation: A chain of 100 amino acids contains 99 peptide bonds. Each hydrolysis reaction breaks one bond and uses one water molecule, which is split to supply the -H and -OH added to the products, so 99 water molecules are used.

questions.stem: A student measures the diameter of a cell as 7 µm. What is this diameter in nanometres?

options.text: 70 nm, because each prefix is ten times the next
7000 nm, because one micrometre is 1000 nanometres
0.007 nm, because a smaller unit means a smaller number
7 000 000 nm, because a micrometre is 10⁻³ of a metre

questions.explanation: 1 µm = 10⁻⁶ m and 1 nm = 10⁻⁹ m, so 1 µm = 1000 nm. The length is unchanged; it is expressed in a smaller unit, so the number is larger: 7 × 1000 = 7000 nm.

questions.stem: Why is the digestion of a polymer into its monomers described as a hydrolysis reaction?

options.text: Water acts only as the solvent in which enzymes break the polymer into its monomers
Water molecules are split, and the -H and -OH produced are added to the monomers
Breaking the bonds between the monomers releases the energy that was stored in those bonds
Water molecules are released as each bond between neighbouring monomers is broken

questions.explanation: Hydrolysis means splitting with water. For each bond broken, one water molecule is split; its -H is added to one product and its -OH to the other, so the water is incorporated into the monomers.

questions.stem: Which statement about the SI prefixes kilo, centi, milli, micro and nano is correct?

options.text: Their meanings were discovered by scientists measuring natural objects
Each prefix is one tenth of the prefix that comes before it
Their meanings are conventions fixed by international agreement
"micro" means one thousandth, and "milli" means one millionth

questions.explanation: The values of the SI prefixes are scientific conventions agreed internationally so that a measurement means the same thing to every scientist. They are agreed, not discovered, which is a nature-of-science point the guide makes explicitly.
